s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: 10-day history of fever
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
past medical history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
white blood cell count: 2.3 × 10^3/μL
hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL
platelet count: 29 × 10^3/μL
C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL
blood culture: negative
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and laboratory findings such as a low white blood cell count and elevated C-reactive protein are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The skin biopsy findings of an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myeloid sarcoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of multiple myeloma, the skin biopsy findings do not show evidence of myeloid sarcoma, which is typically characterized by a dense infiltrate of immature myeloid cells.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy did not show evidence of leukemia cutis, which is typically characterized by a dense infiltrate of leukemic cells in the skin.

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of amyloid deposits in the skin biopsy, which is a hallmark of amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Anemia
rejected.why: While the patient has anemia, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's symptoms and skin biopsy findings.
